security_audit.summary: Four script-loading findings expose the normal integration risk of executing mutable third-party JavaScript with page privileges. The remaining 30 static findings concern Markdown formatting, documentation links, or configuration references, not shell execution or reconnaissance. A separate semantic finding identifies guidance that weakens Content Security Policy; no evidence found of prompt injection or intentional credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The CSP guidance permits unrestricted inline scripts and styles.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer the documented external script form or a nonce or hash for inline scripts. Document stricter style handling instead of broadly recommending unsafe-inline.

remediation.issue: The widget loads mutable third-party JavaScript with page privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Document this trust boundary and require site-owner approval. Offer an immutable, integrity-checked asset if supported, and review deployment on sensitive pages.

content.user_title: Add an Asyntai Chatbot to Your Website
content.value_statement: Adding support chat requires choosing the correct installation method for each website stack. This skill guides Asyntai widget setup, placement, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Locate an existing widget ID or request it from the user, with optional retrieval through a connected Asyntai MCP server.
Identify the website stack from project configuration and choose the corresponding integration instructions.
Provide shared-layout installation guidance for HTML, Next.js, Vite, SvelteKit, Angular, and server templates.
Find hosted-platform installation links and package integration guides for supported site builders and documentation tools.
Check for duplicate widget scripts, inspect browser errors, and troubleshoot Content Security Policy restrictions.
Explain dashboard steps for adding knowledge sources and configuring the chatbot name, colors, and greeting.
limitations: Requires an Asyntai account and a valid widget ID for a working installation.
Loads externally hosted JavaScript and relies on the Asyntai service; it does not provide a local chatbot backend.
Hosted-platform installations require user access to the platform administration interface.
Dashboard automation depends on a connected Asyntai MCP server; the skill does not bundle that server.

use_cases.title: Integrate Support Chat into a Web Application
use_cases.description: Add one shared widget to a Next.js or Vite application and check that it appears across routes.

use_cases.title: Install Chat on an Online Store
use_cases.description: Find the Shopify or WordPress installation guide and identify the administration steps needed to enable the widget.

use_cases.title: Add Assistance to a Documentation Site
use_cases.description: Choose a documented integration for Docusaurus, Starlight, or MkDocs and prepare the dashboard knowledge setup.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Installation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add an Asyntai chatbot to my HTML website. Ask for my widget ID and identify where the snippet belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Hosted-Platform Method
prompt_templates.prompt: My store uses Shopify. Find the matching Asyntai installation guide and summarize the admin steps I need to complete.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate with an Existing Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my Next.js project and find any existing Asyntai widget. Add it once using the correct router layout, preserving existing content.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Restricted Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Asyntai installation for duplicate scripts, route coverage, browser errors, and CSP restrictions. Propose fixes without broadly enabling unsafe-inline.

output_examples.input: Where should I add Asyntai in a Next.js App Router project?
output: Use the shared root layout and the Next.js Script component with lazy loading.
Preserve the existing layout and use your real widget ID.
Verify that the widget appears on multiple routes and that only one widget script loads.

output_examples.input: I use Shopify and do not have a widget ID yet.
output: Open the Asyntai dashboard Install page and copy the widget ID from your snippet.
Use the Shopify installation guide linked in the platform references.
Complete the store administration steps, then confirm that the chat button appears.

output_examples.input: The widget is installed, but no chat button appears.
output: Check for a missing widget ID, duplicate installations, and browser-console widget errors.
Review whether Content Security Policy blocks the widget script or service connection.
Prefer the external script form or an approved nonce or hash instead of broadly allowing inline scripts.

best_practices: Use the correct website widget ID and keep only one installation in the shared layout.
Test multiple routes and inspect browser errors after installation.
Review third-party script access and preserve a restrictive Content Security Policy before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Inventing a widget ID or leaving an undisclosed placeholder in a production installation.
Adding the widget separately to every page component and creating duplicate scripts.
Broadly enabling inline scripts to resolve installation errors without reviewing the security impact.

faq.question: Do I need an Asyntai account?
faq.answer: Yes. A working widget needs an account and the website widget ID from the Asyntai dashboard.

faq.question: Which website technologies have installation guidance?
faq.answer: References cover common frontend frameworks, server templates, documentation tools, and hosted platforms such as WordPress, Shopify, Wix, and Webflow.

faq.question: Does this skill run the chatbot locally?
faq.answer: No. It integrates the externally hosted Asyntai widget and service rather than implementing a local model or chatbot backend.

faq.question: Is an Asyntai MCP connection required?
faq.answer: No. You can provide the widget ID manually. A connected MCP server offers an optional way to retrieve website identifiers.

faq.question: Does installing the widget configure its knowledge?
faq.answer: No. Add website pages, files, or text in the Asyntai dashboard and configure the chatbot appearance there.

faq.question: What security considerations apply?
faq.answer: The widget executes third-party JavaScript with page privileges. Review vendor trust and avoid broadly weakening Content Security Policy for installation.
